mappings.questionText: What is React.js and explain its key features including virtual DOM, component-based architecture, and unidirectional data flow?
mappings.answerText: React.js is a JavaScript library developed by Facebook for building user interfaces. It uses a Virtual DOM which is an in-memory representation of the real DOM. Key features include: 1) Virtual DOM for efficient rendering 2) Component-based architecture where UI is split into reusable components 3) Unidirectional data flow using props and state.

mappings.questionText: What is Node.js? How does its event-driven, non-blocking I/O model work?
mappings.answerText: Node.js is a runtime environment that allows JavaScript to run on the server side. It uses an event loop and non-blocking I/O operations. When an async operation is initiated, Node.js registers a callback and moves to the next task. The event loop processes callbacks when operations complete. This allows handling many concurrent connections efficiently.

mappings.questionText: Define REST API and list its key architectural constraints.
mappings.answerText: REST (Representational State Transfer) is an architectural style for distributed hypermedia systems. Key constraints: Stateless, Client-Server separation, Cacheable, Uniform Interface, Layered System, Code on Demand (optional).

What is CSS Flexbox? Explain with a practical use-case.
mappings.answerText: CSS Flexbox is a layout model that allows flexible arrangement of elements. Uses display:flex on container. Practical use: centering elements both horizontally and vertically, creating responsive navigation bars.
